chunks: Ahmad ibn Harun al-Fami, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Jafar al-Himyari narrated to us from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Husayn ibn Ilwan, from Amr ibn Thabit, from Dawud ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Jufi, from Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir from his forefathers, peace be upon them. He said: The Messenger of Allah, blessings of Allah be upon him and his family, said to al-Husayn, peace be upon him:

O Husayn! A man called Zayd will come forth from your loins. He and his companions will surpass the necks of the people on the Day of Resurrection, shining with radiant marks, entering Paradise without judgment.

key_terms.صلب: sulb -- loins; denoting direct lineage and descent
key_terms.غرا محجلين: ghurran muhajjalin -- shining with white marks on the forehead, hands, and feet; a prophetic description of believers who will be recognizable on the Day of Judgment by the luminous traces of their ablution

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about Zayd ibn Ali and his entry to Paradise on the Day of Resurrection?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) addressed Imam al-Husayn (AS) with a prophecy about Zayd, a descendant from his lineage. Zayd and his companions would surpass all people on the Day of Resurrection with radiant marks of faith (ghurr muhajjalin), entering Paradise without judgment. This hadith, narrated through Imam al-Baqir and transmitted through multiple reliable narrators, honors Zayd ibn Ali, the grandson of Imam al-Husayn, who led a revolt against the Umayyads and is venerated for his sacrifice.
word_analysis: shining (with a white mark on the forehead)
with radiant marks (on hands and feet)
